scope: Isolated S1 dead event loop send checkpoint. A new probe ends the event loop of a child frame for real, by unwinding its script thread or sending SIGKILL to its content process, and sends to the frame's pipeline inside one constellation request, so the panic report or lifeline cannot be read first. Two new cases show that the failed send alone recovers the frame, with one notice, an intact parent, and no second recovery. A serialization error to a live event loop is documented as not producible without a contrived engine change. The parts now have 52, 12, and 33 cases. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.

configuration.part_check: Each part runs as its own fixture process. Each part must print exactly its own case markers, ending with its summary marker, and the summary must report its own case count. Each repeat must then cover 64 cases in single-process mode or 97 cases in multiprocess mode, each once.
configuration.notice_check: Every contained case captures the parent's frame notices inside the barrier, while the parent's script thread still waits and the frame cannot navigate. It requires exactly one notice that names the parent's identity, exactly the failed frame's browsing context and failed pipeline, and the exact reason. The failed pipeline is the frame's current pipeline, or the pending pipeline for a failed pending or first navigation. After the error page, the late data, and a 300-millisecond settle, the parent still has exactly one notice. The parent-loop popup, the child-site popup, and the independent view have none. In the same-site pending cases, the parent's own document fails, and neither the parent nor the parent-loop popup has a notice.
configuration.send_check: frame-send-failure loads a cross-site child alone in its own event loop. Inside the parent's barrier, the probe closes the constellation's channel to that event loop and sends one GetTitle message through send_message_to_pipeline. The send fails with the channel's own error. No script thread unwinds and no process exits. The frame's crash details and the notice reason must begin with "Send failed (", which only handle_send_error builds.
configuration.history_check: javascript-url-history-crash-recovery loads a start page and a source page, replaces the source entry with a javascript: URL result, and loads a next page, for three entries. The next page's script thread unwinds. The crash page must report two entries. Back must reach the start page, forward must restore the crash page, and back must reach the start page again. The result text and marker never appear, and every earlier identity is stale.
configuration.dead_send_check: frame-send-dead-thread (frames part, both modes) and frame-send-dead-process (processes part, multiprocess) load a cross-site child alone in its own event loop. Inside the parent's barrier, one probe request ends the child's event loop for real, by the existing script-thread crash message or by SIGKILL to the child's content process, and then calls send_message_to_pipeline with a GetTitle message every two milliseconds until the frame's pipeline is gone or three seconds pass. The constellation handles the request on its own thread, so the panic report and the process lifeline wait in their queues. The probe must report that the frame runs in another event loop than the parent and that a real send failed and closed the pipeline. The frame's crash details and the one notice must begin with "Send failed (", and the parent's other checks match frame-send-failure. After release, error page, late data, and 300 milliseconds, the parent has exactly one notice. The panic report or lifeline then finds no pipeline of the dead event loop.
configuration.group_check: frame-siblings-failure and frame-nested-failure, with their process exit and kill variants, load a parent that runs in another event loop than the failed frames. The siblings parent has a healthy same-origin frame in the parent's own event loop, then two frames of one cross-site origin. The nested parent has one cross-site frame that contains a frame of its own origin. Before the failure, the new probe must show every frame live with no crash details and no pending pipeline, the failed frames in the newest frame's event loop, and, for siblings, the healthy frame in another loop. Inside the parent's barrier the notice must have arrived exactly once, naming the parent's identity and exactly the outermost failed frames with their failed pipelines, in any order, with the exact reason. The failed pipelines must be closed, the healthy frame's record must be unchanged, and the parent must have no revocation, crash notification, or terminal callback. After release, all eight callbacks must succeed in the same document. Each outermost failed frame must then have a new live pipeline with crash details that begin with the reason, in an event loop other than the failed one, with distinct pipelines. A nested frame's browsing context must be absent. The parent's view of its frames, its readiness, and its notices must not change after 300 milliseconds. Reload must load every frame again without crash details, and a new URL must recover.

engine_patch.change: One experimental probe: WebView::fail_dead_frame_send_for_document_scope_probe, the EmbedderToConstellationMessage::FailDeadFrameSendForDocumentScopeProbe message, its constellation handler, its tracing target, and ProcessManager::pid_of. With a script-thread unwind the handler sends the existing crash message to the newest child frame's pipeline. With a kill it looks up the content process of the frame's event loop and sends SIGKILL, and it requires multiprocess mode. It then sends GetTitle through send_message_to_pipeline every two milliseconds, for at most three seconds, until the pipeline is gone, and replies with whether the frame runs in another event loop and whether the pipeline closed. Hunk headers were recounted by a script that reproduced the previous patch's headers exactly before the edit. No notice, containment, recovery, or send-error behavior changed.

fixture_changes: ParseFailure gains DeadThreadSend and DeadProcessSend, with is_send, reason, reported, how, and wait. The three functions that reject a failed send now reject all send variants.
frame_path_failure handles both new variants for FramePath::Loaded and requires that the probe reported a failed send.
frame-send-dead-thread joins the frames part. frame-send-dead-process joins the processes part.
The runner case lists, scope text, and runner test counts change to 52, 12, and 33 cases, with 64 shared and 97 multiprocess cases.
findings: The current patch already meets the contract for a really dead event loop. A send that fails against a dead script thread or a killed content process before the panic report or lifeline is read stays inside the frame: one notice, an intact parent and popups, one error page that replaces the child, and no second recovery or notice. No patch behavior needed to change.

In single-process mode the dead script thread's receiver is gone and the send error is Disconnected. In multiprocess mode the send error is SerializationError("Error in IO: Bogus destination port..") for both the unwound script thread and the killed process, so this IPC layer reports a dead peer with the SerializationError variant.

The order is deterministic only because the probe holds the constellation's thread in one request. In a real run, a report or lifeline that is handled first closes the pipelines, and a later send finds no pipeline and returns. The negative control shows that the fixture detects the other order.

A serialization error to a live event loop was investigated and not produced. The servo-constellation, servo-constellation-traits, and servo-script-traits sources have no hand-written Serialize implementation, so a failing serialization would need a message type that the engine does not have. The case stays open.

The previous-send-error-rule control confirms that both new cases exercise the engine's send-error rule. Without it, the single-process dead script thread revokes the healthy parent, and in multiprocess mode the failed send no longer closes the frame's pipeline.

timing_observations.note: The runner times each part's whole process, including engine startup and shutdown. The multiprocess frames part grew from 28.5 to 28.7 seconds to 31.3 to 31.6 seconds, and the processes part from 18.0 to 18.3 seconds to 18.9 to 19.0 seconds. The multiprocess frames part's new case waits for the dead script thread's process port to fail. The documents part has no new case. This checkpoint keeps all fixture and runner deadlines. The margins to the 80-second fixture deadline are about 42, 48, and 61 seconds for the documents, frames, and processes parts.

negative_controls.variation: The final patch, with the probe's send loop removed from the copied constellation handler. The handler ends the frame's event loop and replies at once, so the constellation returns to its queues and reads the panic report or the lifeline before any send. Everything else, including the fixture, is final.

engine_overrides.servo-constellation/constellation.rs: Edited in the preparation's copied sources after the final patch applied. See engine_override_note.

negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, the frames part passes the nine earlier cases and fails at frame-send-dead-thread with 'No send to the dead event loop failed within the probe: Some(false)'. In multiprocess mode, the processes part passes thirty-two cases and fails at frame-send-dead-process with the same error. The documents part passes in every run. All three runs of each mode fail the same way.
negative_controls.interpretation: The dead event loop cases require that a real send fails first. If the panic report or the lifeline wins, the existing recovery handles the failure and the send path never runs, so the cases fail rather than pass by another route. This control shows that the fixture detects the other order. It does not test a patch fix, because the patch needed none.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The dead event loop cases cover a single loaded child. A group of frames has no send fixture, and no fixture checks a send that fails while the parent's own document is in the failed event loop.

The probe keeps the constellation in one request until the first send fails. A report or lifeline that is handled first is the other order, which existing process and script-thread cases cover with the reason that names the report or lifeline.
The other callers of handle_send_error have no fixture: pipeline creation, frame navigation and load sends to a parent pipeline, and focus sends.
A serialization error to a live event loop has no fixture and no honest way to produce one without an engine change.
A frame inside a frame whose own parent is healthy, and a nested failure whose inner frame runs in a different event loop than its failed parent, have no fixture.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
